name: CapCut Speed Match To Beat
use_when: A short-form, AMV, sports, or montage clip needs an action pose, impact, transformation, or reveal to land on a music beat.
A time-remapped or slowed source clip can be sped up without losing the action's readability.
A slowed alignment window is needed for a character detail, eye overlay, or power effect to match the visible beat.
Transitions will be added later and the clip duration needs to line up with the music first.
avoid_when: The speed change makes the action unreadable, jittery, or emotionally wrong.
Dialogue, lip sync, or source audio timing must remain natural.
The editor has not marked the target beat or action frame.

timeline_pattern.pattern: choose_action_clip -> mark_song_beat -> identify_action_peak -> adjust_speed -> preview_on_beat -> repeat_for_sequence -> transition_pass
timeline_pattern.beat_marker_rule: Add beat markers before repeating the workflow across clips so speed decisions are made against visible cue points.
timeline_pattern.speed_rule: There is no universal speed value; adjust per clip until the action peak reaches the beat.
timeline_pattern.alignment_window_rule: If an overlay must track a small detail such as an eye, slow or speed-adjust the source before the overlay pass, then recheck that the transformed moment still lands on the beat.
timeline_pattern.sequence_rule: Preview adjacent clips after speed changes so the beat grid feels intentional across the whole run.

motion.rule: Speed changes should make the action feel sharper while preserving the important pose, impact, or direction.

keyframe_values.sync_tolerance: For high-energy AMV-style edits, the action peak should land within 1-2 frames of the intended beat when practical.
keyframe_values.preview_range: Review at least the outgoing clip, the synced clip, and the next cut before locking the speed.
keyframe_values.transition_handles: Keep enough clip duration or handles for transition effects after speed matching.

sound.rule: Use the song beat as the primary timing reference, then add SFX only after the visual hit is locked.

captions.rule: Avoid speed changes that push action under captions or make caption timing feel disconnected from the beat.

color.rule: No required color rule; preserve action readability during any later flashes, glow, or color effects.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use trim plus setpts expressions such as setpts=PTS/speed for visual-only clips, then align the rendered segment against beat-frame metadata.
implementation.remotion: Store sourceInFrame, actionPeakFrame, targetBeatFrame, and playbackRate; compute the clip start or playbackRate so the peak lands on the beat.
implementation.blender: Use speed control strips or time remapping in the VSE, then add markers for beat and action peak.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Select the clip, use Speed, move the speed slider forward or backward, and preview until the action peak lands on the song beat.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Speed/Duration or Time Remapping with sequence markers on the beat and action peak; ripple or slip the clip until the hit lands.

common_mistakes: Using the same speed value on every clip instead of matching each action beat.
Applying a Twixtor-style slow effect directly and building overlays before checking whether the result still matches the beat.
Forgetting beat markers and judging sync by memory.
Speeding up a clip so much that the viewer cannot read the action.
Locking speed before checking whether transitions still have usable handles.
Adding SFX before the visual hit is locked.
qc: Does the action peak land within the intended beat tolerance?
Are beat markers present before multiple clips are speed-matched?
Can the action still be read at delivery size after the speed change?
Do adjacent clips feel musically connected rather than individually guessed?
Are enough handles left for transition effects?
